Ruby, Rails, Puma, and PostgreSQL are installed. If you need anything else, install it yourself.

The owner needs help. Add an `agent` role and let admins invite other admins or agents:

```http
POST /api/v1/invitations

{"invitation":{"email":"sam@example.test","role":"agent"}}
```

Return an `invitation` and email a link to `/accept-invitation?account=acme&token=TOKEN` on the
frontend. Let admins list and inspect invitations, resend them with `POST /invitations/:id/resend`,
and revoke them with `DELETE /invitations/:id`. Track pending, accepted, revoked, and expired
invitations. Don't create competing invitations or let customer registration take a pending invite's email.
List invitations by ID ascending.

The acceptance screen uses `POST /invitation_previews` with
`{"invitation_preview":{"token":"TOKEN"}}` to show the invited email, role, business name, subdomain,
and expiry inside `invitation_preview`. Then it submits:

```http
POST /api/v1/invitation_acceptances

{"invitation_acceptance":{"token":"TOKEN","name":"Sam","password":"my-team-password"}}
```

Return `user` and `account`; Sam can sign in without another verification email.

Admins also need `GET /users`, `GET /users/:id`, and `PATCH /users/:id`. Include `suspended` on users
and support `{"user":{"suspended":true}}`. Suspension revokes sessions and clears assignments.
Don't let admins suspend the last active admin. Filter users by role or suspension, and invitations
by status. `GET /staff` supplies active staff choices for assignment controls.
List users and staff by ID ascending.

Staff can assign tickets with `{"ticket":{"assignee_id":12}}` or clear them with null. Include
`assignee_id` and the assignee's ID/name on tickets. Both admins and agents can work on the business's
tickets, but only admins manage people.

Add private notes through the existing comment input, for example
`{"ticket":{"comment":{"body":"Checking this with billing.","public":false}}}`.
Internal activity must not change the customer-facing request.

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Helpdesk API

Rails API-only backend for a helpdesk SaaS. The frontend is a separate app and
talks to this service over JSON under `/api/v1`.

## Setup

```sh
export DATABASE_URL="postgresql:///helpdesk_development?host=/var/lib/postgresql"
bin/rails db:prepare
bin/rails server -p 3000        # Puma
```

Tests use their own database. Point `DATABASE_URL` at it for the test run:

```sh
DATABASE_URL="postgresql:///helpdesk_test?host=/var/lib/postgresql" RAILS_ENV=test bin/rails db:create db:schema:load
DATABASE_URL="postgresql:///helpdesk_test?host=/var/lib/postgresql" bin/rails test
```

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | none | PostgreSQL connection |
| `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL` | `http://localhost:3001` | Base of verification and reset links, and the only CORS origin allowed |
| `HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM` | `support@example.test` | Sender address for all email |
| `SMTP_ADDRESS`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | — | Production SMTP. `SMTP_ADDRESS` is required, so production fails to boot without it |
| `SECRET_KEY_BASE` | — | Required in production by Rails 8, even though the API uses no cookies |

In development, mail is written to `tmp/mails/`.

Mail is sent through Active Job. The default `async` adapter runs jobs inside the web
process and loses queued mail if the process restarts. Configure a persistent queue
adapter before going live.

## Conventions

- Every request is JSON. Successful responses are the resource objects. Errors look like
  `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "details": {...}}}`.
- `X-Helpdesk-Account: <subdomain>` selects the business. Sign-in, email verification,
  password reset requests and `GET /portal` require it. Signed-in endpoints accept it
  and reject a token used with a different business (`403 wrong_account`).
- Signed-in endpoints use `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Auth | Body |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/api/v1/account/create` | none | `{"account":{"name","subdomain","admin":{"name","email","password"}}}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions` | header | `{"session":{"email","password"}}` |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/session` | bearer | — |
| GET | `/api/v1/me` | bearer | — |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/me` | bearer | `{"user":{"name"}}` |
| PUT | `/api/v1/me/password` | bearer | `{"password_change":{"current_password","password"}}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/email_verifications` | header | `{"email_verification":{"email"}}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm` | none | `{"email_verification":{"token"}}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/password_resets` | header | `{"password_reset":{"email"}}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/password_resets/confirm` | none | `{"password_reset":{"token","password"}}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/portal` | header | — |
| POST | `/api/v1/registrations` | header | `{"user":{"name","email","password"}}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/requests` | bearer | — (paginated) |
| POST | `/api/v1/requests` | bearer | `{"request":{"subject","comment":{"body"}}}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/requests/:id` | bearer | — |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/requests/:id` | bearer | `{"request":{"comment":{"body"},"status":"solved"}}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/requests/:id/comments` | bearer | — (paginated) |
| GET | `/api/v1/tickets` | bearer, staff | — (paginated) |
| GET | `/api/v1/tickets/:id` | bearer, staff | — |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/tickets/:id` | bearer, staff | `{"ticket":{"comment":{"body","public"},"status":"open\|pending\|solved"}}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/tickets/:id/comments` | bearer, staff | — (paginated) |
| GET | `/api/v1/account` | bearer | — |
| POST | `/api/v1/account/cancel` | bearer, owner | — |
| POST | `/api/v1/account/reactivate` | bearer, owner | — |

Emailed links point at the frontend:

- `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL/verify-email?account=ACME&token=TOKEN`
- `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL/reset-password?account=ACME&token=TOKEN`

Lifetimes: verification links last 3 days, reset links 1 hour. Requesting a new link
replaces the previous one.

## Requests and tickets

Customers work with **requests**, at `/api/v1/requests`. Staff work with the same records as
**tickets**, at `/api/v1/tickets`. Customers can only see their own requests. Staff can see
every request in their business. Another business's records always look missing (`404`).

- A new request is `open`. Its first comment comes with the request.
- Responses return records under `request` or `ticket`, and lists under the plural name
  (`requests`, `tickets`, `comments`). A request has `id`, `subject`, `status`,
  `requester_id`, `created_at` and `updated_at`. A ticket also has the requester as
  `{id, name, email}`.
- A comment has `id`, `body`, `public`, `author` (`{id, name}`) and `created_at`.
  Customers only see public comments. Comments are listed oldest first.
- **Customer replies** `PATCH /requests/:id` with an optional `comment` and an optional
  `status`. A customer can only set `status` to `solved`. A reply reopens a `pending` or
  `solved` request, unless the same update marks it solved. Sending neither a comment nor a
  status is a `422`.
- **Staff replies** `PATCH /tickets/:id` with an optional `comment` and an optional `status`
  (`open`, `pending` or `solved`). A reply on its own does not change the status. A comment
  can set `public: false` to make a private note, which customers never see.
- Replies do not send email yet.

Lists are paginated with `page` (default 1) and `per_page` (default 25, at most 100). They
return `count`, `page`, `per_page`, `next_page` and `previous_page` next to the records. A
`page` or `per_page` that is not a whole number of 1 or more returns `400 invalid_pagination`.
Lists are ordered by recent activity, so the request or ticket with the newest reply or
status change comes first.

## Accounts and roles

- Roles are `admin` (the owner), `agent` and `customer`. Staff are the owner and agents.
- Customers register through `POST /api/v1/registrations` with the business header. They
  always get the `customer` role, and use the same verification, sign-in, profile and
  password flows as everyone else. Registration is refused for a cancelled business.
- The admin who registers a business is its **owner**. Only an admin can cancel or
  reactivate the account.
- Owners must verify their email before they can sign in.
- Changing a password, or completing a password reset, signs out every session.
- **Cancelling** revokes every session in the business and blocks ordinary access. Only
  the owner can still sign in, and only to reactivate or view the account. Reactivation
  is allowed for 90 days after cancellation.
- Accounts still cancelled after 90 days are permanently deleted, with their users and
  sessions, by:

  ```sh
  bin/rails helpdesk:purge_cancelled_accounts
  ```

  Schedule this daily (cron, a scheduler, or a job runner).

class Account < ApplicationRecord
  # A cancelled account can be reactivated for this long. After that it is purged.
  CANCELLATION_WINDOW = 90.days
  SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT = /\A[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?\z/
  RESERVED_SUBDOMAINS = %w[api app admin www mail].freeze

  # Raised when a lifecycle change is not allowed. `code` is a stable API error code.
  class StateError < StandardError
    attr_reader :code

    def initialize(code, message)
      @code = code
      super(message)
    end
  end

  has_many :users, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :requests, dependent: :destroy

  normalizes :subdomain, with: ->(value) { value.strip.downcase }

  validates :name, presence: true, length: { maximum: 120 }
  validates :subdomain,
            presence: true,
            length: { maximum: 63 },
            format: { with: SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT, message: "may only use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens" },
            uniqueness: true
  validate :subdomain_not_reserved

  scope :cancelled_before, ->(time) { where(cancelled_at: ..time) }

  def cancelled?
    cancelled_at.present?
  end

  def reactivatable?(now: Time.current)
    cancelled? && cancelled_at > now - CANCELLATION_WINDOW
  end

  def reactivate_by
    cancelled_at + CANCELLATION_WINDOW if cancelled?
  end

  # Marks the account cancelled and signs out every user in it.
  def cancel!(now: Time.current)
    with_lock do
      raise StateError.new("already_cancelled", "This account is already cancelled.") if cancelled?

      update!(cancelled_at: now)
      Session.where(user_id: users.select(:id)).delete_all
    end
  end

  def reactivate!(now: Time.current)
    with_lock do
      raise StateError.new("not_cancelled", "This account is not cancelled.") unless cancelled?
      raise StateError.new("reactivation_window_closed", "This account was cancelled more than 90 days ago and can no longer be reactivated.") unless reactivatable?(now: now)

      update!(cancelled_at: nil)
    end
  end

  # Permanently deletes accounts cancelled more than CANCELLATION_WINDOW ago, with
  # all their data. Returns the number of accounts deleted.
  def self.purge_cancelled!(now: Time.current)
    cutoff = now - CANCELLATION_WINDOW

    cancelled_before(cutoff).pluck(:id).count do |id|
      transaction do
        # Re-check under a row lock: the owner may have reactivated since the scan.
        account = lock.cancelled_before(cutoff).find_by(id: id)
        next false unless account

        account.destroy!
        true
      end
    end
  end

  def as_api_json
    {
      id: id,
      name: name,
      subdomain: subdomain,
      status: cancelled? ? "cancelled" : "active",
      cancelled_at: cancelled_at,
      reactivate_by: reactivate_by,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  private

  def subdomain_not_reserved
    errors.add(:subdomain, "is reserved") if RESERVED_SUBDOMAINS.include?(subdomain)
  end
end

# A signed-in session. The client holds the raw bearer token; only its SHA-256
# digest is stored, so a database leak does not expose usable tokens.
class Session < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :user

  # The raw token. Set only on the object returned by start_for; never persisted.
  attr_accessor :token

  def self.start_for(user)
    raw = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)
    session = create!(user: user, token_digest: digest(raw))
    session.token = raw
    session
  end

  # Returns the session for a raw bearer token, with its user and account loaded.
  def self.lookup(raw)
    return if raw.blank?

    includes(user: :account).find_by(token_digest: digest(raw))
  end

  def self.digest(raw)
    Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw)
  end
end

# One-time links sent by email. Only one token per user and purpose exists at a
# time, so requesting a new link invalidates the previous one.
class UserToken < ApplicationRecord
  LIFETIMES = {
    "email_verification" => 3.days,
    "password_reset" => 1.hour
  }.freeze

  belongs_to :user

  validates :purpose, inclusion: { in: LIFETIMES.keys }

  # Replaces any earlier token for this user and purpose. Returns the raw token
  # for the email link; the database keeps only its digest.
  def self.issue!(user, purpose)
    purpose = purpose.to_s
    raw = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)

    transaction do
      user.user_tokens.where(purpose: purpose).delete_all
      user.user_tokens.create!(
        purpose: purpose,
        token_digest: digest(raw),
        expires_at: LIFETIMES.fetch(purpose).from_now
      )
    end

    raw
  end

  # Returns the unexpired token record matching a raw token, or nil.
  def self.redeem(purpose, raw)
    return if raw.blank?

    record = find_by(purpose: purpose.to_s, token_digest: digest(raw))
    record if record && record.expires_at > Time.current
  end

  def self.digest(raw)
    Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw)
  end
end

# Resolves the business a request is about from the X-Helpdesk-Account header.
module AccountContext
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  private

  def requested_subdomain
    request.headers["X-Helpdesk-Account"].to_s.strip.downcase.presence
  end

  # For public endpoints that need to know the business (sign-in, portal, ...).
  def load_account_from_header!
    subdomain = requested_subdomain
    return render_error(400, "account_required", "Send the X-Helpdesk-Account header with the business subdomain.") if subdomain.nil?

    @account = Account.find_by(subdomain: subdomain)
    render_error(404, "account_not_found", "No business has that subdomain.") unless @account
  end

  # True when no account header was sent, or the header names this account.
  def requested_account_matches?(account)
    requested_subdomain.nil? || requested_subdomain == account.subdomain
  end

  # Ordinary business access stops once the account is cancelled.
  def require_active_account!
    return unless @account.cancelled?

    render_error(403, "account_cancelled", "This account has been cancelled.")
  end

# Offset pagination for list endpoints: ?page=1&per_page=25.
#
# A page or per_page that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 400. A per_page above
# MAX_PER_PAGE is capped, and the response shows the value actually used.
module Pagination
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  DEFAULT_PER_PAGE = 25
  MAX_PER_PAGE = 100

  class InvalidPage < StandardError; end

  included do
    rescue_from InvalidPage do |error|
      render_error(400, "invalid_pagination", error.message)
    end
  end

  private

  # Returns [records, paging] for one page of the scope. `paging` is the set of fields
  # that go next to the records in the response.
  def paginate(scope)
    page = page_number(:page, default: 1)
    per_page = [page_number(:per_page, default: DEFAULT_PER_PAGE), MAX_PER_PAGE].min

    count = scope.count
    offset = (page - 1) * per_page
    # Skip the query for pages past the end. This also keeps huge page numbers out of SQL.
    records = offset < count ? scope.offset(offset).limit(per_page).to_a : []

    paging = {
      count: count,
      page: page,
      per_page: per_page,
      next_page: page * per_page < count ? page + 1 : nil,
      previous_page: page > 1 ? page - 1 : nil
    }
    [records, paging]
  end

  def page_number(name, default:)
    raw = params[name]
    return default if raw.blank?

    value = Integer(raw.to_s, 10, exception: false)
    raise InvalidPage, "#{name} must be a whole number, 1 or more." if value.nil? || value < 1

    value
  end
end

# Authenticates "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" and sets @current_session,
# @current_user and @account.
module SessionAuthentication
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  private

  def authenticate_session!
    @current_session = Session.lookup(bearer_token)
    unless @current_session
      response.headers["WWW-Authenticate"] = 'Bearer realm="helpdesk"'
      return render_error(401, "unauthorized", "Sign in to continue.")
    end

    @current_user = @current_session.user
    @account = @current_user.account
    return if requested_account_matches?(@account)

    render_error(403, "wrong_account", "This session belongs to a different business.")
  end

  def bearer_token
    scheme, token = request.authorization.to_s.split(" ", 2)
    token.presence if scheme.to_s.casecmp?("Bearer")
  end

  # The owner is the admin who registered the business.
  def require_admin!
    return if @current_user.admin?

    render_error(403, "forbidden", "Only the account owner can do that.")
  end

  # Staff are the owner and agents. Customers use the portal's request endpoints instead.
  def require_staff!
    return if @current_user.staff?

    render_error(403, "forbidden", "Only staff can do that.")
  end
end

      # { account: { name, subdomain, admin: { name, email, password } } }
      def create
        account = Account.new(account_params)
        admin = User.new(admin_params.merge(role: User::ADMIN, account: account))

        unless [account.valid?, admin.valid?].all?
          details = { account: account.errors.to_hash, admin: admin.errors.to_hash }.reject { |_, errors| errors.empty? }
          return render_error(422, "validation_failed", "The business could not be created.", details: details)
        end

        token = nil
        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          account.save!
          admin.save!
          token = UserToken.issue!(admin, :email_verification)
        end
        # Send only after commit, so the link never points at a rolled-back user.
        UserMailer.email_verification(admin, token).deliver_later

        render json: { account: account.as_api_json, user: admin.as_api_json }, status: :created
      rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
        # Lost a race with another signup for the same subdomain or email.
        render_error(422, "validation_failed", "That subdomain or email is already taken.")
      end

      def show
        render json: { account: @account.as_api_json }
      end

      def cancel
        @account.cancel!
        render json: { account: @account.as_api_json }
      rescue Account::StateError => e
        render_error(422, e.code, e.message)
      end

      # POST /api/v1/account/reactivate
      def reactivate
        @account.reactivate!
        render json: { account: @account.as_api_json }
      rescue Account::StateError => e
        render_error(422, e.code, e.message)
      end

        require_envelope(:account).permit(:name, :subdomain)
      end

      def admin_params
        admin = require_envelope(:account).fetch(:admin, nil)
        raise ActionController::ParameterMissing, :admin unless admin.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)

        admin.permit(:name, :email, :password).to_h
      end
    end

    class SessionsController < ApplicationController
      before_action :load_account_from_header!, only: :create
      before_action :authenticate_session!, only: :destroy

      # POST /api/v1/sessions
      # { session: { email, password } } with X-Helpdesk-Account
      def create
        credentials = require_envelope(:session).permit(:email, :password)
        password = credentials[:password].to_s
        user = @account.users.find_by(email: credentials[:email].to_s)
        User.burn_password_check(password) if user.nil?
        return render_error(401, "invalid_credentials", "Email or password is incorrect.") unless user&.authenticate(password)

        # A cancelled account only admits its owner, so they can reactivate it.
        if @account.cancelled? && !(user.admin? && @account.reactivatable?)
          return render_error(403, "account_cancelled", "This account has been cancelled.")
        end
        return render_error(403, "email_not_verified", "Verify your email address before signing in.") unless user.verified?

        session = Session.start_for(user)
        render json: {
          session: { token: session.token, id: session.id, created_at: session.created_at },
          user: user.as_api_json,
          account: @account.as_api_json
        }, status: :created
      end

      # DELETE /api/v1/session
      def destroy
        @current_session.destroy!
        render json: { message: "Signed out." }
      end
    end

module Helpdesk
  # Environment-driven settings. Read at call time so tests and boot order
  # never see stale values.
  module Settings
    DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL = "http://localhost:3001".freeze
    DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM = "support@example.test".freeze

    module_function

    # Base URL of the separate frontend app, without a trailing slash.
    def frontend_url
      (ENV["HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL"].presence || DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL).chomp("/")
    end

    # Scheme, host and port of the frontend, in the form a browser sends in `Origin`.
    def frontend_origin
      uri = URI.parse(frontend_url)
      origin = "#{uri.scheme}://#{uri.host}"
      origin += ":#{uri.port}" unless uri.port == uri.default_port
      origin
    end

    def mail_from
      ENV["HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM"].presence || DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM
    end

    # Link to a page on the frontend, e.g. /verify-email?account=acme&token=...
    def frontend_link(path, params)
      "#{frontend_url}#{path}?#{params.to_query}"
    end
  end
end

module Helpdesk

    ALLOWED_METHODS = "GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS".freeze

module ApiTestHelpers

  def json

  def bearer(token)

  def in_account(subdomain, extra = {})
    { ACCOUNT_HEADER => subdomain }.merge(extra)
  end

  def signup_params(subdomain: "acme", name: "Acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: PASSWORD)
    { account: { name: name, subdomain: subdomain, admin: { name: "Jo", email: email, password: password } } }
  end

  def signup!(**options)
    post "/api/v1/account/create", params: signup_params(**options), as: :json
    assert_response :created, response.body
    json
  end

  def sign_in(email: "jo@acme.test", password: PASSWORD, subdomain: "acme")
    post "/api/v1/sessions",

  # The most recent mail sent to `to`, as a Mail::Message.
  def latest_mail(to)
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.select { |mail| Array(mail.to).include?(to) }.last or
      flunk "no mail was sent to #{to}"
  end

  # Pulls the `token` parameter out of the link in the latest mail to `to`,
  # checking that the link points at the expected frontend page.
  def link_token(to:, path:)
    text = latest_mail(to).body.decoded
    link = text[%r{#{Regexp.escape(Helpdesk::Settings.frontend_url)}#{Regexp.escape(path)}\?\S+}]
    flunk "no #{path} link in mail to #{to}" unless link

    Rack::Utils.parse_query(URI.parse(link).query).fetch("token")
  end

    token = link_token(to: email, path: "/verify-email")
    post "/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm",

I've reproduced the private-note bug: a staff-only note changed the customer's `updated_at`. Here is the plan, based on the spec and the existing code:

- **Data model:** `users.suspended`, a new `invitations` table (status derived from timestamps, token stored as a digest), `requests.assignee_id`, and `accounts.owner_id`.
- **Owner vs. admin:** the README says only the owner can cancel or reactivate, and that only the owner can sign in to a cancelled business. Invited admins would otherwise inherit that power, so I'll track the owner explicitly.
- **Locking:** invitation writes, registrations, and suspensions take the account row lock first, so the "one pending invite per email" and "last active admin" rules hold under concurrency.
- **Private notes:** they shouldn't bump the request's `updated_at` (customer-visible), and neither should assignments.

steps.message: Now the `Invitation` model. It holds the rules: one unresolved invitation per email, no invite for an existing member, status derived from timestamps, and a single-use token stored only as a digest. Expired invitations can be resent or revoked, but accepted and revoked ones cannot.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > app/models/invitation.rb <<'EOF'
# An invitation for someone to join the business as an admin or an agent. The emailed
# link carries a token; the database keeps only its digest.
#
# Status comes from the timestamps:
#   accepted - the invitee signed up through the link
#   revoked  - an admin revoked it
#   expired  - it passed expires_at without being accepted or revoked
#   pending  - none of the above, so the link works
class Invitation < ApplicationRecord
  LIFETIME = 7.days
  ROLES = [User::ADMIN, User::AGENT].freeze

  PENDING = "pending".freeze
  ACCEPTED = "accepted".freeze
  REVOKED = "revoked".freeze
  EXPIRED = "expired".freeze
  STATUSES = [PENDING, ACCEPTED, REVOKED, EXPIRED].freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :invited_by, class_name: "User", optional: true

  normalizes :email, with: ->(value) { value.strip.downcase }

  validates :email,
            presence: true,
            length: { maximum: 255 },
            format: { with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP }
  validates :role, inclusion: { in: ROLES, message: "must be admin or agent" }
  validates :token_digest, :expires_at, presence: true
  # Creating or resending an invitation must not compete with a pending one or a member.
  validate :email_available, on: %i[issue resend]

  # Neither accepted nor revoked. Expiry is checked separately because it depends on the time.
  scope :unresolved, -> { where(accepted_at: nil, revoked_at: nil) }
  scope :pending, ->(now = Time.current) { unresolved.where(arel_table[:expires_at].gt(now)) }
  scope :expired, ->(now = Time.current) { unresolved.where(arel_table[:expires_at].lteq(now)) }
  scope :accepted, -> { where.not(accepted_at: nil) }
  scope :revoked, -> { where(accepted_at: nil).where.not(revoked_at: nil) }

  # Filters by the status names in the API. Statuses are checked in the same order as #status.
  def self.with_status(status, now: Time.current)
    case status
    when PENDING then pending(now)
    when ACCEPTED then accepted
    when REVOKED then revoked
    when EXPIRED then expired(now)
    else raise ArgumentError, "unknown invitation status: #{status}"
    end
  end

  # Returns the invitation for a raw token, whatever its status.
  def self.find_by_token(raw)
    return if raw.blank?

    find_by(token_digest: digest(raw))
  end

  # Invites someone to the business. Returns [invitation, raw_token]; the caller emails the
  # token. Refused while the email belongs to a member or already has a pending invitation.
  def self.issue!(account:, invited_by:, email:, role:, now: Time.current)
    raw = new_token
    invitation = nil

    transaction do
      # Locking the business serializes invitations and registrations, so two requests
      # cannot both pass the checks for the same email.
      account.lock!
      invitation = account.invitations.new(
        invited_by: invited_by,
        email: email,
        role: role,
        token_digest: digest(raw),
        expires_at: now + LIFETIME
      )
      invitation.save!(context: :issue)
    end

    [invitation, raw]
  end

  # True when a pending invitation exists for this email, so customers cannot register with it.
  def self.pending_for_email?(account, email, now: Time.current)
    account.invitations.pending(now).exists?(email: email)
  end

  def self.new_token
    SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)
  end

  def self.digest(raw)
    Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw)
  end

  # Issues a new link that is valid for the full LIFETIME, and stops the old link working.
  # Only pending and expired invitations can be resent. Returns the raw token.
  def resend!(now: Time.current)
    raw = self.class.new_token

    account.with_lock do
      lock!
      ensure_open!
      self.token_digest = self.class.digest(raw)
      self.expires_at = now + LIFETIME
      save!(context: :resend)
    end

    raw
  end

  # Revokes the invitation so its link stops working. Accepted and already revoked
  # invitations cannot be revoked.
  def revoke!(now: Time.current)
    account.with_lock do
      lock!
      ensure_open!
      update!(revoked_at: now)
    end
  end

  # Creates the invitee's account with the invited role and a verified email, and marks the
  # invitation accepted. Returns the new user. If the user is invalid, nothing is saved.
  def accept!(name:, password:, now: Time.current)
    user = nil

    account.with_lock do
      lock!
      ensure_pending!(now: now)
      # The invitation link proves the invitee owns the email, so no verification email is needed.
      user = account.users.create!(name: name, email: email, password: password, role: role, verified_at: now)
      update!(accepted_at: now)
    end

    user
  end

  def status(now: Time.current)
    if accepted?
      ACCEPTED
    elsif revoked?
      REVOKED
    elsif expires_at <= now
      EXPIRED
    else
      PENDING
    end
  end

  def pending?(now: Time.current)
    status(now: now) == PENDING
  end

  def accepted?
    accepted_at.present?
  end

  def revoked?
    revoked_at.present?
  end

  # The admin's view of an invitation. Never includes the token.
  def as_api_json(now: Time.current)
    {
      id: id,
      email: email,
      role: role,
      status: status(now: now),
      expires_at: expires_at,
      accepted_at: accepted_at,
      revoked_at: revoked_at,
      invited_by: invited_by && { id: invited_by.id, name: invited_by.name },
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  # What the acceptance screen shows before the invitee signs up.
  def as_preview_api_json
    {
      email: email,
      role: role,
      business_name: account.name,
      subdomain: account.subdomain,
      expires_at: expires_at
    }
  end

  private

  def ensure_open!
    raise StateError.new("invitation_accepted", "This invitation has already been accepted.") if accepted?
    raise StateError.new("invitation_revoked", "This invitation was revoked. Send a new invitation instead.") if revoked?
  end

  def ensure_pending!(now:)
    ensure_open!
    return if pending?(now: now)

    raise StateError.new("invitation_expired", "This invitation has expired. Ask an admin to send it again.")
  end

  def email_available
    return if email.blank? || account.nil?

    if account.users.exists?(email: email)
      errors.add(:email, "already belongs to someone in this business")
    elsif account.invitations.pending.where(email: email).where.not(id: id).exists?
      errors.add(:email, "already has a pending invitation")
    end
  end
end

cd /app && cat > app/controllers/api/v1/invitations_controller.rb <<'EOF'
module Api
  module V1
    # Admins invite people to join as admins or agents, and manage each invitation until it
    # is accepted.
    class InvitationsController < ApplicationController
      include Pagination

      before_action :authenticate_session!
      before_action :require_active_account!
      before_action :require_admin!
      before_action :load_invitation, only: %i[show resend destroy]

      # GET /api/v1/invitations?status=pending
      # Oldest first. The status filter is pending, accepted, revoked or expired.
      def index
        scope = @account.invitations.includes(:invited_by).order(id: :asc)

        if params[:status].present?
          unless Invitation::STATUSES.include?(params[:status])
            return render_error(400, "invalid_filter", "status must be one of #{Invitation::STATUSES.join(', ')}.")
          end

          scope = scope.with_status(params[:status])
        end

        records, paging = paginate(scope)
        render json: { invitations: records.map(&:as_api_json), **paging }
      end

      # GET /api/v1/invitations/:id
      def show
        render json: { invitation: @invitation.as_api_json }
      end

      # POST /api/v1/invitations
      # { invitation: { email, role: "admin" | "agent" } }
      def create
        attrs = require_envelope(:invitation).permit(:email, :role)

        invitation, token = Invitation.issue!(
          account: @account,
          invited_by: @current_user,
          email: attrs[:email].to_s,
          role: attrs[:role].to_s
        )
        # Send only after commit, so the link never points at a rolled-back invitation.
        InvitationMailer.invitation(invitation, token).deliver_later

        render json: { invitation: invitation.as_api_json }, status: :created
      end

      # POST /api/v1/invitations/:id/resend
      # Sends a new link that replaces the old one and runs for the full lifetime.
      def resend
        token = @invitation.resend!
        InvitationMailer.invitation(@invitation, token).deliver_later

        render json: { invitation: @invitation.as_api_json }
      end

      # DELETE /api/v1/invitations/:id
      # Revokes the invitation so its link stops working. The record stays, as revoked.
      def destroy
        @invitation.revoke!
        render json: { invitation: @invitation.as_api_json }
      end

      private

# Lets the acceptance screen work from the invitation's token alone, with no sign-in. The
# token is the credential, so a token for another business is reported like an unknown one.
module InvitationToken
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  private

  # Loads @invitation and @account from the token in `envelope`, e.g. the body of
  # {"invitation_preview": {"token": ...}}. Renders an error and stops the request if the
  # token is unknown or the business is cancelled.
  def load_invitation_from_token!(envelope)
    token = require_envelope(envelope).require(:token)
    invitation = Invitation.find_by_token(token)
    invitation = nil unless invitation && requested_account_matches?(invitation.account)

    return render_error(422, "invalid_token", "This invitation link is invalid.") unless invitation

    @invitation = invitation
    @account = invitation.account
    require_active_account!
  end
end
EOF

module Api
  module V1
    # Admins manage the people in the business: find them, and suspend or restore them.
    class UsersController < ApplicationController
      include Pagination

      before_action :authenticate_session!
      before_action :require_active_account!
      before_action :require_admin!
      before_action :load_user, only: %i[show update]

      # GET /api/v1/users?role=agent&suspended=true
      # Oldest first.
      def index
        scope = @account.users.order(id: :asc)

        if params[:role].present?
          unless User::ROLES.include?(params[:role])
            return render_error(400, "invalid_filter", "role must be one of #{User::ROLES.join(', ')}.")
          end

          scope = scope.where(role: params[:role])
        end

        if params[:suspended].present?
          suspended = parse_boolean(params[:suspended])
          return render_error(400, "invalid_filter", "suspended must be true or false.") if suspended.nil?

          scope = scope.where(suspended: suspended)
        end

        records, paging = paginate(scope)
        render json: { users: records.map(&:as_api_json), **paging }
      end

      # GET /api/v1/users/:id
      def show
        render json: { user: @user.as_api_json }
      end

      # PATCH /api/v1/users/:id
      # { user: { suspended: true | false } }
      # Suspending signs the user out and unassigns their tickets. The last active admin
      # cannot be suspended.
      def update
        attrs = require_envelope(:user)
        unless attrs.key?(:suspended)
          return render_error(422, "validation_failed", "Only suspended can be changed here.",
                              details: { suspended: ["is required"] })
        end

        suspended = parse_boolean(attrs[:suspended])
        if suspended.nil?
          return render_error(422, "validation_failed", "suspended must be true or false.",
                              details: { suspended: ["must be true or false"] })
        end

        suspended ? @user.suspend! : @user.unsuspend!
        render json: { user: @user.as_api_json }
      end

      private

      def load_user
        @user = @account.users.find_by(id: params[:id])
        render_error(404, "not_found", "No user has that ID.") unless @user
      end
    end
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class UsersTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    @owner_session = owner_session
    @owner_token = @owner_session.dig("session", "token")
    @owner_id = @owner_session.dig("user", "id")
    @agent_session = invited_session!(admin_token: @owner_token, email: "sam@example.test", role: "agent")
    @agent_token = @agent_session.dig("session", "token")
    @agent_id = @agent_session.dig("user", "id")
    @avery = customer_session
    @avery_token = @avery.dig("session", "token")
  end

  def patch_user(id, body, token: @owner_token)
    patch "/api/v1/users/#{id}", params: { user: body }, headers: bearer(token), as: :json
  end

  # --- Listing and inspecting -----------------------------------------------------

  test "admins list everyone oldest first, with suspension on each user" do
    get "/api/v1/users", headers: bearer(@owner_token)

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 3, json["count"]
    users = json.fetch("users")
    assert_equal users.map { |u| u["id"] }.sort, users.map { |u| u["id"] }
    assert_equal [false, false, false], users.map { |u| u["suspended"] }
    assert_equal %w[admin agent customer], users.map { |u| u["role"] }.sort
  end

  test "filters users by role" do
    get "/api/v1/users", params: { role: "agent" }, headers: bearer(@owner_token)

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [@agent_id], json.fetch("users").map { |u| u["id"] }
  end

  test "filters users by suspension" do
    suspend_user!(token: @owner_token, user_id: @agent_id)

    get "/api/v1/users", params: { suspended: "true" }, headers: bearer(@owner_token)
    assert_equal [@agent_id], json.fetch("users").map { |u| u["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/users", params: { suspended: "false" }, headers: bearer(@owner_token)
    assert_equal [@owner_id, @avery.dig("user", "id")].sort, json.fetch("users").map { |u| u["id"] }.sort
  end

  test "an unknown role or a non-boolean suspension filter is a 400" do
    get "/api/v1/users", params: { role: "owner" }, headers: bearer(@owner_token)
    assert_response :bad_request
    assert_equal "invalid_filter", json.dig("error", "code")

    get "/api/v1/users", params: { suspended: "yes" }, headers: bearer(@owner_token)
    assert_response :bad_request
    assert_equal "invalid_filter", json.dig("error", "code")
  end

  test "shows one user, and a user from another business is not found" do
    get "/api/v1/users/#{@agent_id}", headers: bearer(@owner_token)

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "sam@example.test", json.dig("user", "email")
    assert_equal false, json.dig("user", "suspended")

    signup!(subdomain: "globex", name: "Globex", email: "jo@globex.test")
    verify_email!(email: "jo@globex.test", subdomain: "globex")
    globex_token = sign_in!(subdomain: "globex", email: "jo@globex.test").dig("session", "token")

    get "/api/v1/users/#{@agent_id}", headers: bearer(globex_token)
    assert_response :not_found
  end

  test "agents and customers cannot manage people" do
    [@agent_token, @avery_token].each do |token|
      get "/api/v1/users", headers: bearer(token)
      assert_response :forbidden
      get "/api/v1/users/#{@agent_id}", headers: bearer(token)
      assert_response :forbidden
      patch_user(@avery.dig("user", "id"), { suspended: true }, token: token)
      assert_response :forbidden
    end
    assert_equal false, User.find(@avery.dig("user", "id")).suspended?
  end

  # --- Suspending -------------------------------------------------------------------

  test "suspending a user marks them suspended and signs them out everywhere" do
    other_device = sign_in!(email: "sam@example.test").dig("session", "token")

    patch_user(@agent_id, { suspended: true })

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal true, json.dig("user", "suspended")
    assert_equal 0, Session.where(user_id: @agent_id).count

    get "/api/v1/me", headers: bearer(@agent_token)
    assert_response :unauthorized
    get "/api/v1/me", headers: bearer(other_device)
    assert_response :unauthorized
  end

  test "a suspended user cannot sign in" do
    patch_user(@agent_id, { suspended: true })

    sign_in(email: "sam@example.test", password: "my-team-password")

    assert_response :forbidden
    assert_equal "user_suspended", json.dig("error", "code")
  end

  test "a suspended user's bearer token is refused even if a session somehow survived" do
    # Simulate a session that outlived the suspension, e.g. from a race with sign-in.
    User.find(@agent_id).update!(suspended: true)

    get "/api/v1/tickets", headers: bearer(@agent_token)

    assert_response :unauthorized
  end

  test "suspending clears the tickets assigned to the user, without touching the tickets" do
    opened = open_request_for(@avery_token)
    patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{opened['id']}", params: { ticket: { assignee_id: @agent_id } }, headers: bearer(@owner_token), as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    updated_at = Request.find(opened["id"]).updated_at

    travel 1.hour do
      patch_user(@agent_id, { suspended: true })
    end

    assert_nil Request.find(opened["id"]).assignee_id
    assert_equal updated_at.to_i, Request.find(opened["id"]).updated_at.to_i
  end

  test "restoring a user lets them sign in again, without restoring the old sessions" do
    patch_user(@agent_id, { suspended: true })
    patch_user(@agent_id, { suspended: false })

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal false, json.dig("user", "suspended")
    get "/api/v1/me", headers: bearer(@agent_token)
    assert_response :unauthorized

    sign_in!(email: "sam@example.test", password: "my-team-password")
  end

  test "suspending a suspended user is a no-op" do
    patch_user(@agent_id, { suspended: true })

    patch_user(@agent_id, { suspended: true })

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal true, json.dig("user", "suspended")
  end

  test "a PATCH must say whether the user is suspended" do
    patch_user(@agent_id, { name: "Changed" })

    assert_response :unprocessable_content
    assert json.dig("error", "details", "suspended").present?
    assert_equal false, User.find(@agent_id).suspended?
  end

  test "suspended must be true or false, not a guess" do
    patch_user(@agent_id, { suspended: "maybe" })

    assert_response :unprocessable_content
    assert json.dig("error", "details", "suspended").present?
    assert_equal false, User.find(@agent_id).suspended?
  end

  test "a string false is a real false, not a suspension" do
    patch_user(@agent_id, { suspended: "false" })

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal false, json.dig("user", "suspended")
  end

  test "suspending a user in another business is a 404" do
    signup!(subdomain: "globex", name: "Globex", email: "jo@globex.test")
    globex_user = Account.find_by!(subdomain: "globex").users.first

    patch_user(globex_user.id, { suspended: true })

    assert_response :not_found
    assert_equal false, globex_user.reload.suspended?
  end

  # --- The last active admin ----------------------------------------------------------

  test "the last active admin cannot be suspended" do
    patch_user(@owner_id, { suspended: true })

    assert_response :unprocessable_content
    assert_equal "last_active_admin", json.dig("error", "code")
    assert_equal false, User.find(@owner_id).suspended?
  end

  test "an admin can be suspended while another active admin remains" do
    ann = invited_session!(admin_token: @owner_token, email: "ann@example.test", role: "admin")
    ann_id = ann.dig("user", "id")

    patch_user(ann_id, { suspended: true })
    assert_response :ok

    # The owner is now the only active admin, so the owner is protected.
    patch_user(@owner_id, { suspended: true })
    assert_response :unprocessable_content
    assert_equal "last_active_admin", json.dig("error", "code")
  end

  test "a suspended admin does not count as an active admin" do
    ann = invited_session!(admin_token: @owner_token, email: "ann@example.test", role: "admin")
    ann_token = ann.dig("session", "token")
    ann_id = ann.dig("user", "id")
    patch_user(@owner_id, { suspended: true }, token: ann_token) # ann suspends owner, leaving ann the only admin
    assert_response :ok

    patch_user(ann_id, { suspended: true }, token: ann_token)

    assert_response :unprocessable_content
    assert_equal "last_active_admin", json.dig("error", "code")
  end

  test "the last-admin rule does not stop an agent or customer from being suspended" do
    patch_user(@agent_id, { suspended: true })
    assert_response :ok

    patch_user(@avery.dig("user", "id"), { suspended: true })
    assert_response :ok
  end

  # --- Staff choices ----------------------------------------------------------------

  test "staff lists active admins and agents, oldest first, with their names and roles" do
    get "/api/v1/staff", headers: bearer(@agent_token)

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [@owner_id, @agent_id], json.fetch("staff").map { |s| s["id"] }
    assert_equal({ "id" => @agent_id, "name" => "Sam", "role" => "agent" }, json.fetch("staff").last)
    assert_equal 2, json["count"]
  end

  test "staff leaves out suspended users and customers" do
    patch_user(@agent_id, { suspended: true })

    get "/api/v1/staff", headers: bearer(@owner_token)

    assert_equal [@owner_id], json.fetch("staff").map { |s| s["id"] }
  end

  test "customers cannot list staff" do
    get "/api/v1/staff", headers: bearer(@avery_token)

    assert_response :forbidden
  end

  test "staff listing is paginated" do
    get "/api/v1/staff", params: { per_page: 1 }, headers: bearer(@owner_token)

    assert_equal 1, json.fetch("staff").size
    assert_equal 2, json["count"]
    assert_equal 2, json["next_page"]
  end

  private

  def open_request_for(token)
    post "/api/v1/requests", params: { request: { subject: "Receipt", comment: { body: "Broken" } } },
         headers: bearer(token), as: :json
    assert_response :created, response.body
    json.fetch("request")
  end
end

require "test_helper"

# Assignments and private notes are internal. They must never change what the customer
# sees: the request's status, its updated_at, or where it sits in the customer's list.
class TicketAssignmentsTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    @owner_session = owner_session
    @owner_token = @owner_session.dig("session", "token")
    @owner_id = @owner_session.dig("user", "id")
    @agent_session = invited_session!(admin_token: @owner_token, email: "sam@example.test", role: "agent")
    @agent_token = @agent_session.dig("session", "token")
    @agent_id = @agent_session.dig("user", "id")
    @avery_session = customer_session
    @avery_token = @avery_session.dig("session", "token")
    @avery_id = @avery_session.dig("user", "id")
  end

  def open_request(subject: "Receipt", token: @avery_token)
    post "/api/v1/requests", params: { request: { subject: subject, comment: { body: "Broken" } } },
         headers: bearer(token), as: :json
    assert_response :created, response.body
    json.fetch("request")
  end

  def staff_patch(id, ticket, token: @agent_token)
    patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{id}", params: { ticket: ticket }, headers: bearer(token), as: :json
  end

  def customer_view(id)
    get "/api/v1/requests/#{id}", headers: bearer(@avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    json.fetch("request")
  end

  # --- Assigning --------------------------------------------------------------------

  test "staff assign a ticket to a staff member, and the ticket shows the assignee's ID and name" do
    opened = open_request

    staff_patch(opened["id"], { assignee_id: @agent_id })

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal @agent_id, json.dig("ticket", "assignee_id")
    assert_equal({ "id" => @agent_id, "name" => "Sam" }, json.dig("ticket", "assignee"))
  end

  test "an agent can assign a ticket, including to an admin" do
    opened = open_request

    staff_patch(opened["id"], { assignee_id: @owner_id }, token: @agent_token)

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal @owner_id, json.dig("ticket", "assignee_id")
  end

  test "assigning null clears the assignee" do
    opened = open_request
    staff_patch(opened["id"], { assignee_id: @agent_id })

    staff_patch(opened["id"], { assignee_id: nil })

    assert_response :ok
    assert_nil json.dig("ticket", "assignee_id")
    assert_nil json.dig("ticket", "assignee")
    assert_nil Request.find(opened["id"]).assignee_id
  end

  test "the assignee is shown on the ticket list and on a single ticket" do
    opened = open_request

require "test_helper"

class InvitationTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @account = Account.create!(name: "Acme", subdomain: "acme")
    @jo = @account.users.create!(name: "Jo", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password", role: "admin", verified_at: Time.current)
    @now = Time.current
  end

  def issue(email: "sam@example.test", role: "agent", now: @now)
    Invitation.issue!(account: @account, invited_by: @jo, email: email, role: role, now: now)
  end

  test "the raw token is returned once and only its digest is stored" do
    invitation, raw = issue

    assert_equal Invitation.digest(raw), invitation.reload.token_digest
    refute_equal raw, invitation.token_digest
    assert_equal invitation, Invitation.find_by_token(raw)
    assert_nil Invitation.find_by_token("wrong")
    assert_nil Invitation.find_by_token(nil)
  end

  test "status follows the timestamps, and expiry is inclusive at the deadline" do
    invitation, = issue(now: @now)

    assert_equal "pending", invitation.status(now: @now)
    assert_equal "pending", invitation.status(now: invitation.expires_at - 1.second)
    assert_equal "expired", invitation.status(now: invitation.expires_at)
  end

  test "accepted wins over revoked and expired" do
    invitation, = issue(now: @now)
    invitation.update_columns(accepted_at: @now, revoked_at: nil)

    assert_equal "accepted", invitation.status(now: @now + 1.year)
  end

  test "the status scopes agree with the status method" do
    now = @now
    pending, = issue(email: "a@example.test", now: now)
    expired, = issue(email: "b@example.test", now: now - Invitation::LIFETIME - 1.day)
    revoked, = issue(email: "c@example.test", now: now)
    revoked.update_columns(revoked_at: now)
    accepted, = issue(email: "d@example.test", now: now)
    accepted.update_columns(accepted_at: now)

    expected = Invitation.where(account: @account).order(:id).to_h { |i| [i.id, i.status(now: now)] }
    assert_equal({ pending.id => "pending", expired.id => "expired", revoked.id => "revoked", accepted.id => "accepted" }, expected)

    Invitation::STATUSES.each do |status|
      ids = Invitation.where(account: @account).with_status(status, now: now).pluck(:id)
      assert_equal expected.select { |_, s| s == status }.keys.sort, ids.sort, status
    end
  end

  test "an unknown status cannot be filtered on" do
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { Invitation.with_status("lost") }
  end

  test "a second pending invitation for the same email is refused" do
    issue
    error = assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid) { issue(role: "admin") }

    assert_match(/already has a pending invitation/, error.record.errors[:email].first)
  end

  test "an email that already belongs to a member is refused" do
    error = assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid) { issue(email: "jo@acme.test") }

    assert_match(/already belongs to someone/, error.record.errors[:email].first)
  end

  test "roles are limited to admin and agent" do
    error = assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid) { issue(role: "customer") }

    assert_equal ["must be admin or agent"], error.record.errors[:role]
  end

  test "revoked or expired invitations do not block a new one" do
    old, = issue(now: @now - Invitation::LIFETIME - 1.day)
    fresh, = issue(now: @now)

    assert_equal "expired", old.status(now: @now)
    assert_equal "pending", fresh.status(now: @now)
    assert_operator fresh.id, :>, old.id
  end

  test "an expired invitation cannot be accepted, and an accepted one cannot be accepted again" do
    expired, = issue(email: "e@example.test", now: @now - Invitation::LIFETIME - 1.day)
    error = assert_raises(StateError) { expired.accept!(name: "E", password: "my-team-password", now: @now) }
    assert_equal "invitation_expired", error.code

    invitation, = issue(email: "f@example.test", now: @now)
    invitation.accept!(name: "F", password: "my-team-password", now: @now)
    error = assert_raises(StateError) { invitation.accept!(name: "F", password: "my-team-password", now: @now) }
    assert_equal "invitation_accepted", error.code
  end

  test "accepting creates a verified user with the invited role and leaves no partial account on failure" do
    invitation, = issue(role: "admin")

    assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid) { invitation.accept!(name: "", password: "my-team-password") }
    assert_equal "pending", invitation.reload.status
    assert_equal 0, User.where(email: "sam@example.test").count

    user = invitation.accept!(name: "Sam", password: "my-team-password")
    assert_equal "admin", user.role
    assert user.verified?
    assert_equal "accepted", invitation.reload.status
  end

  test "resending issues a new token and a full lifetime" do
    invitation, old_raw = issue(now: @now - 6.days)

    new_raw = invitation.resend!(now: @now)

    assert_nil Invitation.find_by_token(old_raw)
    assert_equal invitation, Invitation.find_by_token(new_raw)
    assert_in_delta (@now + Invitation::LIFETIME).to_f, invitation.reload.expires_at.to_f, 1
  end

  test "a pending invitation blocks customer registration for its email, and others do not" do
    issue
    assert Invitation.pending_for_email?(@account, "sam@example.test")
    refute Invitation.pending_for_email?(@account, "other@example.test")
    refute Invitation.pending_for_email?(Account.create!(name: "Globex", subdomain: "globex"), "sam@example.test")
  end

  test "the API view never includes the token" do
    invitation, raw = issue

    refute_includes invitation.as_api_json.to_s, raw
    refute_includes invitation.as_api_json.keys.map(&:to_s), "token_digest"
  end
end

  def suspend!
    account.with_lock do

      if admin? && account.users.active.where(role: ADMIN).where.not(id: id).none?

        # update_all skips timestamps: unassigning is internal, so the request's updated_at stays put.

    end

  OPEN = "open".freeze
  PENDING = "pending".freeze
  SOLVED = "solved".freeze
  STATUSES = [OPEN, PENDING, SOLVED].freeze
  SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH = 255

  NOT_GIVEN = Object.new.freeze

  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :requests

  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true

  validate :requester_belongs_to_account
  validate :assignee_is_active_staff, if: :assignee_id_changed?

  # Replies and status changes touch the request, so this orders by the latest activity.
  scope :recently_active, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  # Opens a request with its first comment, from the requester. Both or neither are saved.
  def self.submit!(requester:, subject:, body:)
    transaction do
      request = create!(account: requester.account, requester: requester, subject: subject, status: OPEN)
      request.comments.create!(author: requester, body: body, public: true)
      request
    end
  end

  # A reply from the requester: an optional comment and an optional status.
  #
  # Requesters can only mark a request solved. A comment reopens a pending or solved
  # request, unless the same update marks it solved.
  def requester_reply!(author:, body: nil, status: nil)
    invalid!(:base, "Send a comment, a status, or both.") if body.nil? && status.nil?
    invalid!(:status, "can only be set to solved by the requester") if status && status != SOLVED

    with_lock do
      comments.create!(author: author, body: body, public: true) unless body.nil?

      # `status` here is the argument, so the current value is read through self.
      if status == SOLVED
        self.status = SOLVED
      elsif body && self.status != OPEN
        self.status = OPEN
      end
      save!
    end
  end

  # A reply from staff: an optional comment, an optional status and an optional assignee
  # (a user ID, or nil to unassign). A reply on its own does not change the status.
  #
  # Only a status change is customer-visible here. Public comments touch the request on
  # their own. Private notes and assignments leave updated_at alone, so they are invisible
  # to the customer.
  def staff_reply!(author:, body: nil, public: true, status: nil, assignee_id: NOT_GIVEN)
    assigning = !assignee_id.equal?(NOT_GIVEN)
    invalid!(:base, "Send a comment, a status, or an assignee.") if body.nil? && status.nil? && !assigning

    with_lock do
      comments.create!(author: author, body: body, public: public) unless body.nil?
      self.assignee_id = assignee_id if assigning
      self.status = status unless status.nil?
      save!(touch: status_changed?)
    end
  end

  # The customer's view of a request.
  def as_api_json
    {
      id: id,
      subject: subject,
      status: status,
      requester_id: requester_id,

# Authenticates "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" and sets @current_session,
# @current_user and @account.
module SessionAuthentication
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  private

  def authenticate_session!
    @current_session = Session.lookup(bearer_token)
    unless @current_session
      response.headers["WWW-Authenticate"] = 'Bearer realm="helpdesk"'
      return render_error(401, "unauthorized", "Sign in to continue.")
    end

    @current_user = @current_session.user
    @account = @current_user.account
    return if requested_account_matches?(@account)

    render_error(403, "wrong_account", "This session belongs to a different business.")
  end

  def bearer_token
    scheme, token = request.authorization.to_s.split(" ", 2)
    token.presence if scheme.to_s.casecmp?("Bearer")
  end

  # Admins manage people and invitations.
  def require_admin!
    return if @current_user.admin?

    render_error(403, "forbidden", "Only admins can do that.")
  end

  # The owner is the admin who registered the business. Only the owner can cancel or
  # reactivate it.
  def require_owner!
    return if @current_user.owner?

    render_error(403, "forbidden", "Only the account owner can do that.")
  end

  # Staff are the owner and agents. Customers use the portal's request endpoints instead.
  def require_staff!
    return if @current_user.staff?

    render_error(403, "forbidden", "Only staff can do that.")
  end
end

# A signed-in session. The client holds the raw bearer token; only its SHA-256
# digest is stored, so a database leak does not expose usable tokens.
class Session < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :user

  # The raw token. Set only on the object returned by start_for; never persisted.
  attr_accessor :token

  def self.start_for(user)
    raw = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)
    session = create!(user: user, token_digest: digest(raw))
    session.token = raw
    session
  end

  # Returns the session for a raw bearer token, with its user and account loaded.
  # A suspended user's session is not valid, even if one somehow survived the suspension.
  def self.lookup(raw)
    return if raw.blank?

    session = includes(user: :account).find_by(token_digest: digest(raw))
    session unless session&.user&.suspended?
  end

  def self.digest(raw)
    Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw)
  end
end

  ```sh
  bin/rails helpdesk:purge_cancelled_accounts
  ```

  Schedule this daily (cron, a scheduler, or a job runner).

## Invitations

Admins add people by invitation. Only admins and agents can be invited, and an invitee
joins with the invited role.

- `POST /api/v1/invitations` returns the `invitation` and emails the invitee a link to
  `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL/accept-invitation?account=ACME&token=TOKEN`. The token is only in
  that email, never in the API.
- An invitation has `id`, `email`, `role`, `status`, `expires_at`, `accepted_at`,
  `revoked_at`, `invited_by` (`{id, name}`), `created_at` and `updated_at`.
- **Status** is `pending`, `accepted`, `revoked` or `expired`. Accepted and revoked win
  over expired. Pending invitations expire 7 days after they were sent.
- **One open invitation per email.** An invitation is refused while the email belongs to a
  member, or while another invitation for it is pending (`validation_failed`, with the
  reason under `details.email`). Expired and revoked invitations do not block a new one.
- **Customer registration** is refused for an email with a pending invitation. The message
  is worded so it does not reveal the invitation.
- `POST /invitations/:id/resend` sends a new link that replaces the old one and runs for a
  full lifetime. It works for pending and expired invitations. Accepted and revoked
  invitations cannot be resent (`invitation_accepted`, `invitation_revoked`).
- `DELETE /invitations/:id` revokes the invitation so its link stops working. The record
  stays, as `revoked`. Pending and expired invitations can be revoked. Accepted ones cannot,
  and an invitation cannot be revoked twice.
- `GET /invitations` lists oldest first, filtered with `?status=`. `GET /invitations/:id`
  shows one. Both are admin-only.
- **Acceptance** has two steps, with no sign-in. `POST /invitation_previews` returns
  `invitation_preview` with `email`, `role`, `business_name`, `subdomain` and `expires_at`.
  `POST /invitation_acceptances` with a `name` and `password` creates the user with the
  invited role and a verified email, so the invitee signs in without another verification
  email. It returns `user` and `account` (`201`). A link works once. A failed attempt (for
  example, a short password) leaves the invitation pending.
- An unknown or mismatched token is `invalid_token`. Accepted, revoked and expired
  invitations return `invitation_accepted`, `invitation_revoked` and `invitation_expired`.
  Cancelled businesses return `403 account_cancelled`.

## People

Only admins manage people. Agents and customers get `403`.

- `GET /users` lists everyone in the business, oldest first. Filter with
  `?role=admin|agent|customer` and `?suspended=true|false`. `GET /users/:id` shows one user.
  Users include `suspended`.
- `PATCH /users/:id` with `{"user":{"suspended":true}}` suspends a user, and
  `{"user":{"suspended":false}}` restores them. `suspended` is required (`422` without it),
  and other fields in the body are ignored. Changing a user's role is not supported yet.
- **Suspending** signs the user out everywhere, so their bearer tokens stop working. They
  cannot sign in (`403 user_suspended`). Tickets assigned to them become unassigned. Their
  request's `updated_at` does not change, since that is internal activity.
- **Restoring** lets the user sign in again. Their old sessions are not restored.
- **The last active admin** cannot be suspended (`422 last_active_admin`). Suspended admins do
  not count as active.
- `GET /staff` lists the active admins and agents, oldest first, as `{id, name, role}`. Staff
  use it for assignment controls. Agents and admins can both call it.

# An invitation for someone to join the business as an admin or an agent. The emailed
# link carries a token; the database keeps only its digest.
#
# Status comes from the timestamps:
#   accepted - the invitee signed up through the link
#   revoked  - an admin revoked it
#   expired  - it passed expires_at without being accepted or revoked
#   pending  - none of the above, so the link works
class Invitation < ApplicationRecord
  LIFETIME = 7.days
  ROLES = [User::ADMIN, User::AGENT].freeze

  PENDING = "pending".freeze
  ACCEPTED = "accepted".freeze
  REVOKED = "revoked".freeze
  EXPIRED = "expired".freeze
  STATUSES = [PENDING, ACCEPTED, REVOKED, EXPIRED].freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :invited_by, class_name: "User", optional: true

  normalizes :email, with: ->(value) { value.strip.downcase }

  validates :email,
            presence: true,
            length: { maximum: 255 },
            format: { with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP }
  validates :role, inclusion: { in: ROLES, message: "must be admin or agent" }
  validates :token_digest, :expires_at, presence: true
  # Creating or resending an invitation must not compete with a pending one or a member.
  validate :email_available, on: %i[issue resend]

  # Neither accepted nor revoked. Expiry is checked separately because it depends on the time.
  scope :unresolved, -> { where(accepted_at: nil, revoked_at: nil) }
  scope :pending, ->(now = Time.current) { unresolved.where(arel_table[:expires_at].gt(now)) }
  scope :expired, ->(now = Time.current) { unresolved.where(arel_table[:expires_at].lteq(now)) }
  scope :accepted, -> { where.not(accepted_at: nil) }
  scope :revoked, -> { where(accepted_at: nil).where.not(revoked_at: nil) }

  # Filters by the status names in the API. Statuses are checked in the same order as #status.
  def self.with_status(status, now: Time.current)
    case status
    when PENDING then pending(now)
    when ACCEPTED then accepted
    when REVOKED then revoked
    when EXPIRED then expired(now)
    else raise ArgumentError, "unknown invitation status: #{status}"
    end
  end

  # Returns the invitation for a raw token, whatever its status.
  def self.find_by_token(raw)
    return if raw.blank?

    find_by(token_digest: digest(raw))
  end

  # Invites someone to the business. Returns [invitation, raw_token]; the caller emails the
  # token. Refused while the email belongs to a member or already has a pending invitation.
  def self.issue!(account:, invited_by:, email:, role:, now: Time.current)
"
}

  def self.issue!(account:, invited_by:, email:, role:, now: Time.current)
    raw = new_token
    invitation = nil

    transaction do
      # Locking the business serializes invitations and registrations, so two requests
      # cannot both pass the checks for the same email.
      account.lock!
      invitation = account.invitations.new(
        invited_by: invited_by,
        email: email,
        role: role,
        token_digest: digest(raw),
        expires_at: now + LIFETIME
      )
      invitation.save!(context: :issue)
    end

    [invitation, raw]
  end

  # True when a pending invitation exists for this email, so customers cannot register with it.
  def self.pending_for_email?(account, email, now: Time.current)
    account.invitations.pending(now).exists?(email: email)
  end

  def self.new_token
    SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)
  end

  def self.digest(raw)
    Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw)
  end

  # Issues a new link that is valid for the full LIFETIME, and stops the old link working.
  # Only pending and expired invitations can be resent. Returns the raw token.
  def resend!(now: Time.current)
    raw = self.class.new_token

    account.with_lock do
      lock!
      ensure_open!
      self.token_digest = self.class.digest(raw)
      self.expires_at = now + LIFETIME
      save!(context: :resend)
    end

    raw
  end

  # Revokes the invitation so its link stops working. Accepted and already revoked
  # invitations cannot be revoked.
  def revoke!(now: Time.current)
    account.with_lock do
      lock!
      ensure_open!
      update!(revoked_at: now)
    end
  end

  # Creates the invitee's account with the invited role and a verified email, and marks the
  # invitation accepted. Returns the new user. If the user is invalid, nothing is saved.
  def accept!(name:, password:, now: Time.current)
    user = nil

    account.with_lock do
      lock!
      ensure_pending!(now: now)
      # The invitation link proves the invitee owns the email, so no verification email is needed.
      user = account.users.create!(name: name, email: email, password: password, role: role, verified_at: now)
      update!(accepted_at: now)
    end

    user
  end

  def status(now: Time.current)
    if accepted?
      ACCEPTED
    elsif revoked?

import json, re, subprocess, sys, glob, urllib.request, time

BASE = "http://localhost:3055/api/v1"

def call(method, path, body=None, token=None, account=None):
    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
    if token: headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
    if account: headers["X-Helpdesk-Account"] = account
    data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + path, data=data, method=method, headers=headers)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as r:
            return r.status, json.loads(r.read() or b"null")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, json.loads(e.read() or b"null")

def latest_link(path_fragment, to):
    # Dev mail goes to tmp/mails; the async adapter may take a moment.
    for _ in range(50):
        files = sorted(glob.glob("/app/tmp/mails/*"), key=lambda f: __import__("os").path.getmtime(f))
        for f in reversed(files):
            text = open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
            if f"To: {to}" in text or to in text:
                text = text.replace("=\n", "")
                m = re.search(r"https?://\S*" + re.escape(path_fragment) + r"\?\S+", text)
                if m:
                    return m.group(0).strip().rstrip(".")
        time.sleep(0.2)
    raise SystemExit(f"no mail for {to}")

def token_of(link):
    from urllib.parse import urlparse, parse_qs
    return parse_qs(urlparse(link).query)["token"][0]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    pass
EOF

# Lets the acceptance screen work from the invitation's token alone, with no sign-in. The
# token is the credential, so a token for another business is reported like an unknown one.
module InvitationToken
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  private

  # Loads @invitation and @account from the token in `envelope`, e.g. the body of
  # {"invitation_preview": {"token": ...}}. Renders an error and stops the request if the
  # token is unknown or the business is cancelled.
  def load_invitation_from_token!(envelope)
    token = require_envelope(envelope).require(:token)
    invitation = Invitation.find_by_token(token)
    invitation = nil unless invitation && requested_account_matches?(invitation.account)

    return render_error(422, "invalid_token", "This invitation link is invalid.") unless invitation

    @invitation = invitation
    @account = invitation.account
    require_active_account!
  end

steps.message: The test scaffolding is clean now. Reviewing the concurrency story turned up one real gap. Assigning a ticket checks that the assignee isn't suspended, but that check runs under the request's row lock only. A suspension could commit between the check and the save, leaving a suspended person assigned, which breaks the "suspension clears assignments" rule. Suspension takes the business lock first, so an assignment should take the same lock first, in the same order, to avoid deadlocks.

steps.message: Those 73 tests pass. Now I'll check the race concretely. A test transaction can't see data from other threads, so this runs as a standalone script against the test database: it repeatedly races suspension against assignment on real connections, then checks the invariant (a suspended user is never left assigned) and counts any deadlock errors.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > /tmp/repro/race.rb <<'EOF'
# Races suspension against assignment on separate DB connections, many times.
# Invariant: after both finish, no request is assigned to a suspended user.
suffix = SecureRandom.hex(4)
violations = 0
errors = Hash.new(0)
ok = 0

account = Account.create!(name: "Race #{suffix}", subdomain: "race#{suffix}")
owner = account.users.create!(name: "Owner", email: "o@#{suffix}.test", password: "my-first-password", role: "admin", verified_at: Time.current)
account.update!(owner: owner)
agent = account.users.create!(name: "Agent", email: "a@#{suffix}.test", password: "my-first-password", role: "agent", verified_at: Time.current)
customer = account.users.create!(name: "Cust", email: "c@#{suffix}.test", password: "my-first-password", role: "customer", verified_at: Time.current)

200.times do |i|
  # A second admin, so the last-admin guard does not interfere with the race.
  request = Request.submit!(requester: customer, subject: "R#{i}", body: "b")
  agent.update!(suspended: false)
  barrier = Queue.new
  threads = [
    Thread.new do
      ActiveRecord::Base.connection_pool.with_connection do
        barrier.pop
        begin
          User.find(agent.id).suspend!
        rescue => e
          errors[e.class.name] += 1
        end
      end
    end,
    Thread.new do
      ActiveRecord::Base.connection_pool.with_connection do
        barrier.pop
        begin
          Request.find(request.id).staff_reply!(author: owner, assignee_id: agent.id)
        rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid
          # Refused because the agent was already suspended: fine.
        rescue => e
          errors[e.class.name] += 1
        end
      end
    end
  ]
  2.times { barrier << :go }
  threads.each(&:join)

  request.reload
  agent.reload
  if request.assignee_id && agent.suspended?
    violations += 1
  else
    ok += 1
  end
end

steps.message:
Everything is in its final state. The full suite passed after my last code change, the server is stopped, and the development database is clean.

## Summary

The invitation, people, and assignment features are built to the spec, and the existing 162 tests still pass alongside 108 new ones (270 total, 0 failures). I also ran the whole flow against a real Puma server with the development mailer.

### What's in place
- **Invitations:** `POST/GET/DELETE /invitations`, `GET /invitations/:id`, and `POST /invitations/:id/resend`. Status (pending, accepted, revoked, expired) is derived from timestamps, and `?status=` filters it. The emailed link is `/accept-invitation?account=…&token=…`. Tokens are stored only as digests and never appear in API responses.
- **Acceptance:** `POST /invitation_previews` and `POST /invitation_acceptances` return the specified shapes. Accepting creates a verified user, so no verification email is sent, and the link works once.
- **People:** `GET /users`, `GET /users/:id`, and `PATCH /users/:id` with `suspended`. Suspension signs the user out, blocks sign-in, and unassigns their tickets. `GET /staff` lists active staff.
- **Tickets:** `assignee_id` is settable or clearable, and the ticket shows `assignee: {id, name}`. Assignees must be active staff in the same business.

### Bugs found and fixed along the way
- **Private notes changed what customers see.** Every comment touched the request, so an internal note moved the customer's `updated_at` and list position. Only public replies and status changes count now. Assignment changes don't touch the request either.
- **Assignment race.** Suspension could commit between the assignee check and the save, leaving a suspended person assigned. Assignments now take the business lock, the same order suspension uses. A race script showed 199/200 violations without the lock and 0/200 with it.

### Decisions to review
- **Owner-only cancel.** The README makes cancel, reactivate, and cancelled-account sign-in owner-only, which invited admins would otherwise inherit. I added `accounts.owner_id`, backfilled to the first admin, so invited admins can't cancel the business.
- **Invitation lifetime is 7 days**, which the spec didn't specify. Resend renews it and replaces the link. Revoking an expired invitation is allowed so admins can close it out.
- **Response details I chose:** acceptance returns `201` with no session (the user then signs in normally). `DELETE` returns `200` with the invitation. Error codes are `last_active_admin`, `user_suspended`, `invalid_token`, `invitation_accepted|revoked|expired`, and `invalid_filter`.
- **Registration refusal** for a pending invitee's email uses neutral wording, so the response doesn't reveal the invitation.
- **`PATCH /users/:id`** changes only `suspended`. Other fields are ignored, which matches the existing convention. Role changes are not supported.
- **Concurrency** is handled with row and business locks. The races I could test were checked manually, but there's no automated concurrency test.

### Open risk
An invited admin can suspend the owner. The last-admin rule keeps one active admin, but if that admin is the only one left, they alone can restore the owner. The spec didn't cover owner protection, so I didn't add it. Tell me if you want it.

### Not covered
- Inviting an email that is already a customer is refused. There's no way to promote a customer to staff yet.
- The existing ticket-keys test was updated, since tickets now include `assignee_id` and `assignee` by design.

Migrations `20261123060001`–`…0004` run and roll back cleanly, and `db/schema.rb` is regenerated. `README.md` documents the new endpoints, rules, and error codes.
